title: Implementation of 3D-printed pharmaceuticals in geriatric/neurological care concepts: opportunities, barriers and perspectives
summary: Swallowing difficulties are more common in advanced age or in patients with neurological disorders. This also makes medication intake more difficult. They are treated with the standard therapy of amlodipine 5 mg, ramipril 5 mg, spironolactone 12.5 mg, or spironolactone 25 mg. Until now, these medications were only available as conventional tablets. Currently, there is the option of replacing these tablets with a 3D-printed, semi-solid drop containing the appropriate active ingredient. This study aims to determine whether patients with swallowing difficulties find taking 3D-printed drops easier and more comfortable. Additionally, it will investigate whether administration time can be saved. In the future, the 3D-printed tablet will offer the possibility of individualizing medication dosages for each patient.

interventions.name:
Observational study: Questionnaire taken after taking the 3D-printed tablet compared to a standard tablet

Repeated intake/one-time questionnaire survey

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
patients with prescription for amlodipine 5 mg or ramipril 5 mg or spironolactone 12,5 mg or spironolactone 25 mg;
hospitalized patients
Exclusion criteria:
Age < 50 years
